title: Recitals Identifying and Defining the Underlying Lease Being Amended
where_to_look: Recitals or Background section at the front of an amendment, renewal, or extension, before the operative terms.
required: Open the amendment with recitals that identify the underlying lease by title, date, parties, and premises, roll every prior amendment and related memorandum into one defined term, and state the purpose of this amendment.
fallback: Accept shorter recitals that identify the underlying lease by date alone, provided the defined term expressly sweeps in all prior amendments and modifications and the amendment's purpose appears in the first operative section.
escalate_if: An instrument that changes term, premises, or rent under an existing tenancy is drafted as a freestanding lease with no recitals identifying the lease it amends.
flag_if: The document moves from the party paragraph straight into operative terms with no recitals or background section.
The recitals name the original lease but omit a prior amendment, commencement date memorandum, or errata addendum.
The lease defined term used in the recitals differs from the term used in the operative sections.
A recital date for the underlying lease or a prior amendment conflicts with the referenced document or another language version.
The recitals describe the premises or square footage differently from the underlying lease.
preferred_language: Landlord and Tenant are parties to that certain lease dated [date], together with every amendment, commencement date memorandum, errata addendum, and other modification of it executed by the parties, collectively the "Lease," demising the premises described in the Lease, and the parties now desire to amend the Lease as expressly set forth in this Amendment. Each capitalized term used but not defined in this Amendment has the meaning given to it in the Lease, and the Lease remains in full force and effect as amended hereby.
confidence_note: Based on 9 findings across 9 counterparties, all moving in the same direction toward fuller recitals identifying the underlying lease, though most were medium rather than high significance.
matching_clause_names: Background/Recitals - Item 1 (Initial Lease / Initial Leased Property description)

title: Effective / Execution Date and Document Identification
where_to_look: Cover page caption, preamble, and opening recitals identifying the instrument, the parties, and its effective date.
required: Require the preamble to state one specific effective date and to identify the instrument and every prior document it amends.
fallback: Accept an effective date fixed by the last signature, provided the caption names the instrument correctly and the recitals identify each prior agreement by title and date.
escalate_if: A blank, backdated, or internally conflicting effective date, or a preamble naming the wrong Marmon contracting entity, goes to an attorney.
flag_if: The effective date is blank or left as a fill-in placeholder.
The preamble date conflicts with the signature-page, DocuSign, or notarial date.
The caption reads as a new lease while the recitals describe an amendment, renewal, or extension.
The recitals reference a prior agreement without stating its title and date.
The Marmon entity or signatory named in the preamble differs from the signature page.
The contract or document number on the cover page differs from the number used elsewhere in the document.
preferred_language: This Agreement is effective as of the date on which the last Party executes it (the "Effective Date"), and the Effective Date controls for all purposes notwithstanding any other date appearing on the cover page, in the signature blocks, or in any notarial certificate. The recitals identify by title and date the prior agreement that this Agreement amends, renews, or extends, together with each amendment to that agreement then in effect.
confidence_note: Based on 7 findings across 7 counterparties, consistent in direction toward a corrected date and an accurately captioned instrument, though three of the findings reflect document-pairing artifacts rather than true negotiated redlines.

title: Order of Precedence, No Novation, and Survival of Unamended Terms
where_to_look: Closing or miscellaneous provisions of any amendment, renewal, or letter extension to an existing lease.
required: State expressly that the amendment controls over conflicting lease terms, that all unamended terms survive, and that no novation occurs.
fallback: Accept precedence plus a savings clause confirming unamended terms remain in force, so long as every guaranty, security deposit, and letter of credit under the original lease is separately reaffirmed in writing.
escalate_if: The amendment supersedes or replaces the underlying lease, or is silent on novation where the deal relies on a guaranty or posted security.
flag_if: The amendment contains no clause confirming that unamended lease terms remain in full force and effect.
No order-of-precedence sentence resolves conflicts between the amendment and the underlying lease.
The precedence language gives the underlying lease or a prior amendment priority over the current document.
A renewal or extension in a civil-law jurisdiction lacks an express no-novation statement.
A substantive lease provision drops out at the same location where a savings clause is inserted.
preferred_language: Except as expressly amended by this Amendment, all terms and conditions of the Lease and of each prior amendment remain in full force and effect and are hereby ratified and confirmed. In the event of any conflict or ambiguity between this Amendment and the Lease or any prior amendment, this Amendment shall govern and control. This Amendment is supplemental to the Lease and shall not constitute a novation, extinguishment, or replacement of the Lease, of any prior amendment, or of any guaranty or security granted in connection therewith.
confidence_note: Based on 4 findings across 3 counterparties with consistent direction, strongest on precedence and no-novation language in renewals and extensions.
matching_clause_names: Terms of the Lease / Order of Precedence

title: Identity and Substitution of Contracting Parties, Successors, and Guarantors
where_to_look: Preamble party identification, notice addresses, and any guaranty or extension-letter recital naming the parties.
required: Identify each party and guarantor by exact current legal name, entity form, and state of organization, and recite the successor-in-interest chain back to the party of record.
fallback: Accept a trade name or former name only where the same provision also states the party's exact legal name, entity form, state of organization, and its status as successor to the original party of record.
escalate_if: A different landlord, tenant, or guarantor entity is substituted without written proof of the successor's title and authority to bind.
flag_if: A party is named without its entity form or state of organization.
A party is identified by a trade name or a former corporate name only.
The named landlord differs from the landlord of record under the prior lease or amendments.
The guarantor entity or the guarantor's signing officer differs from the existing guaranty.
Notice provisions do not copy Marmon Holdings in-house legal at its own address.
preferred_language: Each party is identified herein by its exact current legal name, entity form, and state of organization, and each party represents that it is the party of record under the Lease or the successor-in-interest to that party, holding all right, title, and interest of that party. Any change in the identity of Landlord, Tenant, or Guarantor is effective only upon delivery of a written instrument to the other party identifying the successor entity, its entity form and state of organization, and the instrument by which it acquired that interest.
confidence_note: Based on 4 findings across 3 counterparties, consistent in direction on entity-identity accuracy and successor recitals, though one landlord-substitution finding may reflect a document-pairing artifact rather than a negotiated change.
matching_clause_names: Preamble / Recitals (Parties and Reference to Lease)

title: Corporate Capacity, Authority, and Formation Representations
where_to_look: Opening recitals and party-representation clauses, including renewals and amendments that shorten the original recitals.
required: Each party expressly represents its due organization, good standing, and the current unrevoked authority of its signatory.
fallback: Accept dropping formation, notarial, and registry detail where the renewal or amendment expressly reaffirms the capacity and authority representations of the original agreement as of the new effective date.
escalate_if: Never accept a renewal or amendment that carries no capacity or authority representation and no reaffirmation of the original.
flag_if: Recitals name a signatory or attorney-in-fact without stating that the authority remains unrevoked.
A renewal or amendment deletes the original formation and authority recitals without reaffirming them.
The entity named in the recitals differs from the entity named in the signature block.
Title to the property sits with a trustee or beneficiary that is not a party to the agreement.
No party representation addresses good standing or power to enter the agreement.
preferred_language: Each party represents and warrants that it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization, that it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and that the individual executing this Agreement on its behalf holds authority that has not been revoked, modified, or limited. Each party reaffirms these representations as of the Effective Date.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings drawn from a single lease renewal with one counterparty, both of medium significance and both resting on ambiguous diff evidence, so this rule is provisional.

title: Lease Term Length, Commencement, and Expiration Dates
where_to_look: Term or Lease Grant section, plus any amendment that restates the term, commencement date, or expiration date.
required: Fix the term with express commencement and expiration dates and a firm initial term of no more than three years. Place any additional years in tenant-side renewal options.
fallback: Accept a five-year firm term where the commencement and expiration dates are both stated expressly and the lease grants at least one tenant renewal option.
escalate_if: The term lacks a stated expiration date, or it binds the tenant beyond five years with no renewal option and no early exit right.
flag_if: The term is defined by duration only, with no stated expiration date.
Commencement is tied to an event that the lease does not define.
The firm initial term exceeds three years.
The stated commencement date does not match the date possession is actually delivered.
Renewal or extension years are folded into the firm term instead of stated as options.
preferred_language: Term. The term of this Lease commences on the Commencement Date, being the date Landlord delivers exclusive possession of the Premises to Tenant, and expires at 11:59 p.m. on the last day of the thirty-sixth (36th) full calendar month thereafter. Landlord and Tenant shall confirm both dates in writing, and this Lease shall state each date expressly. Occupancy beyond the expiration date arises only through Tenant's exercise of a renewal option granted in this Lease.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings across 3 counterparties, all rated high significance and consistent in direction toward shorter firm terms with expressly dated boundaries, though one of the three may reflect a comparison across different underlying deals.

title: Renewal and Extension Options: Fix Dates and Renewal Rent
where_to_look: Term, Renewal Option, or Extended Term sections, and any amendment or notice exercising a renewal option.
required: State express commencement and expiration dates for each renewal or extension term and fix the renewal rent in the document itself. All other lease terms carry forward unchanged.
fallback: Accept renewal rent set by a stated schedule with fixed annual escalation of no more than two percent, or a renewal duration and rent set by cross-reference to a named section of the existing lease. Accept a renewal term whose expiration is fixed by a stated number of months running from the commencement date.
escalate_if: Renewal rent is set at fair market value, by landlord determination, or by future agreement, or a renewal term commences with no stated expiration date.
flag_if: Renewal rent is stated as fair market value or is set by the landlord.
A renewal or extended term gives a commencement date without an expiration date.
The number or duration of remaining renewal options is deleted or left blank.
Renewal rent is left to future agreement between the parties.
Annual rent escalation during a renewal term exceeds two percent.
preferred_language: Tenant shall have the option to extend the Term for one additional period commencing on the day after the then-current Term expires and expiring on the fifth anniversary of that commencement date, exercisable by written notice to Landlord given at least ninety (90) days before the then-current Term expires. Base Rent during the extension period shall equal the Base Rent in effect immediately before that period commenced, and all other terms and conditions of this Lease shall continue unchanged. Any remaining extension options granted to Tenant survive the exercise of this option.
confidence_note: Based on 7 findings across 6 counterparties, consistent direction toward express renewal dates and rent fixed in the document, though two findings rest on fragmentary extracted text.

title: Base Rent Amount, Rent Schedule, and Escalation
where_to_look: Base Rent or Rent clause and any attached rent schedule, including renewal, extension, and amendment rent terms.
required: Fix Base Rent for every period in a fully restated schedule stating each period dates and exact monthly amount, with escalations set as stated dollar figures.
fallback: Accept a percentage escalator only where it is capped at a stated maximum, applies no more than once a year, and takes effect only after written notice. Any superseded rent schedule is deleted and restated in full rather than amended by cross-reference.
escalate_if: Never accept a landlord right to adjust Base Rent unilaterally, an uncapped or market-reset escalator, or a rent figure whose words and numerals disagree.
flag_if: The written-out rent amount and the numeral do not match.
A renewal or extension term has no stated rent amount.
An escalation is expressed without a stated cap or ceiling.
Landlord may adjust Base Rent without notice to Tenant.
A rent schedule is changed by cross-reference without being deleted and restated in full.
preferred_language: Tenant shall pay Base Rent in the amounts and for the periods set forth in the Base Rent Schedule attached to this Lease, which is restated in full and supersedes every prior rent schedule. The commencement date, expiration date, and monthly Base Rent for each period are as stated in that Schedule. Where an amount appears in both words and numerals, the numerals control. Base Rent shall not increase except as expressly stated in the Schedule, and Landlord shall have no right to adjust Base Rent unilaterally.
confidence_note: Based on 8 findings across 8 counterparties, all high significance and consistent in direction, including two where the written words and the numeral for rent disagreed after the change.

title: Rent Payment Timing, Proration, and Collection Mechanics
where_to_look: Rent and service charge payment terms clause, including any proration provision for partial first and last months.
required: Require day-count proration of rent and service charges for partial first and last months, with one fixed monthly due date.
fallback: Accept rent payable monthly in advance without demand, and service charges recoverable as rent in arrears, provided proration for partial months is expressly stated and the tenant keeps a written notice and cure period before default remedies attach.
escalate_if: A waiver of all deduction and set-off rights is paired with rent acceleration or with default remedies that attach without notice or cure.
flag_if: The lease sets no proration method for a partial first or last calendar month.
Rent is payable in advance without demand and without any grace period.
Service charges are recoverable as if they were rent in arrears.
Rent is payable without any deduction, set-off, or counterclaim.
The first payment is due on the earlier of execution or the commencement date.
preferred_language: Tenant shall pay Monthly Base Rent and the monthly service charge in advance on the first day of each calendar month of the Lease Term. If the Lease Term begins on a day other than the first day of a calendar month, or ends on a day other than the last day of a calendar month, Monthly Base Rent and the monthly service charge for that beginning or ending month shall be prorated based upon the number of days in such month occurring within the Lease Term.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties with mixed direction, one adding tenant-favorable proration and one accepting landlord collection mechanics, so this rule is provisional.

title: Rent Credits, Abatement, and Rent-Free Periods
where_to_look: Rent commencement and rent credit provisions, and the definitions of Fitting-Out Period and Rent Free Period.
required: Obtain a defined rent-free period covering the full fit-out window and a rent credit stated as a fixed amount applied to named rent installments.
fallback: Accept a shorter rent-free period fixed by calendar dates, provided the credit amount and the specific rent installments it offsets are stated in the document and any unused balance carries forward.
escalate_if: Never accept abatement or credit language that Landlord can revoke, recapture, or reduce on Tenant default without attorney approval.
flag_if: Fitting-Out Period or Rent Free Period is defined as "Not Applicable".
Rent commencement is the same date as possession or lease commencement.
A rent credit or concession is referenced without a stated dollar amount.
The rent credit is not tied to identified rent installments or calendar months.
Abatement or credit is forfeited, repayable, or suspended on Tenant default.
preferred_language: Rent Credit and Rent-Free Period. No Base Rent, additional rent, or service charge shall accrue or be payable during the Fitting-Out Period, which runs from delivery of possession of the Premises through the Rent Commencement Date. Landlord grants Tenant a rent credit of $[amount], which Tenant shall apply against the Base Rent installment first coming due after the Rent Commencement Date, with any unapplied balance carried forward to successive installments until exhausted. Such rent-free period and credit are unconditional and shall not be revoked, recaptured, or reduced.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties, consistent direction but a thin evidence base.
matching_clause_names: Definitions – Fitting-Out Period / Rent Free Period

title: Security Deposit and Advance Rental (Amount, Application, and Refund)
where_to_look: The security deposit, rental deposit, and rental-in-advance clauses, and the deposit figures in the lease schedule.
required: Cap the security deposit at one month's gross rent and require it refunded in full within thirty days after the Term ends, less only sums actually owed.
fallback: Accept up to two months' gross rent held as deposit or advance rental, with refund within one month after the Term ends and deductions limited to sums actually due and itemized in writing.
escalate_if: Never accept forfeiture of the deposit on any breach, refund left to Landlord discretion, or a lease with no outer date for return.
flag_if: The deposit or advance rental exceeds two months' gross rent.
The lease sets no outer date for returning the deposit after the Term ends.
The deposit is stated to be forfeited or non-refundable on Tenant breach.
Deductions from the deposit are not limited to amounts actually due to the Landlord.
The deposit amount written in words does not match the numeral.
preferred_language: Tenant shall pay Landlord a security deposit equal to one (1) month's gross rent, to be held as security for Tenant's performance and not applied as payment of rent or any other charge. Landlord shall refund the deposit in full within thirty (30) days after the expiry or earlier determination of the Term, subject to deduction only for sums then actually due and owing to Landlord and itemized in a written statement delivered to Tenant. The deposit shall not otherwise be forfeited on account of any breach by Tenant.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings from a single landlord across two leases, both marked high significance and pointing the same direction on deposit size and refund mechanics, but one turns on a words-versus-numerals discrepancy, so this rule is provisional.
matching_clause_names: Rental in Advance / Landlord's Remedies for Breach

title: Scope of Operating Expense and Tax Pass-Throughs (Inclusions and Exclusions)
where_to_look: The Operating Expenses definition with its inclusion and exclusion lists, and the definition of Taxes.
required: Limit Operating Expenses to routine, non-capital costs of operating the Building itself, and narrow the Taxes definition to real estate taxes only.
fallback: Accept a broader inclusion list only with express exclusions for capital expenditures, structural, roof and parking replacement, Landlord income and rent-based taxes, personnel not dedicated solely to the Building, latent defects, Hazardous Substances remediation, and duplicate charges. Permitted capital items must be amortized over useful life with Tenant paying only the annual share.
escalate_if: Do not accept pass-through of structural, roof or Building-system replacement costs, or a Taxes definition reaching Landlord income or rent-based taxes, without attorney approval.
flag_if: Operating Expenses include maintenance, repair or replacement of the roof, roof membrane, structure, foundation or exterior walls.
Taxes is defined as any tax rather than real estate taxes only.
Capital improvements or capital expenditures are chargeable to Tenant without an amortization limit.
Operating Expenses reach Park-wide, common-area or off-Building improvements such as paving, roads and landscaping.
Landlord salaries, wages or benefits are charged without a limit to personnel working solely for the Building.
preferred_language: Operating Expenses shall mean the actual costs of routine, non-capital operation, maintenance and repair of the Building. Operating Expenses exclude capital improvements and capital expenditures, including roof and roof membrane replacement and parking area repaving; costs to maintain, repair or replace the structure, foundation, exterior walls, roof or Building systems; salaries and benefits of personnel not working solely for the Building; costs to cure latent defects or violations of law or to remediate Hazardous Substances; and any duplication of charges. Taxes means real estate taxes only, and excludes any tax based on Rent and any income tax imposed on Landlord.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings, both marked high significance and moving in the same direction, but both from a single lease negotiation with one counterparty, so the direction is clear while the breadth of the pattern is provisional.

title: Management Fee Caps and Capital-Cost Recovery / Amortization
where_to_look: Operating Expenses definition and its exclusions, covering the management fee component and capital-cost amortization language.
required: Cap the property management and administrative fee at 3% of Operating Expenses. Include law-compliance capital costs only where the law first takes effect after the lease date, amortized over the item's full useful life.
fallback: Accept a management fee cap of 4% of Operating Expenses computed without including the fee itself. Accept law-compliance capital costs amortized over the lesser of useful life or fifteen years where the work also produces a net reduction in Operating Expenses.
escalate_if: Uncapped management fees payable to a Landlord affiliate, or pass-through of capital costs curing pre-existing legal non-compliance, require attorney approval.
flag_if: Operating Expenses include property management fees with no stated percentage cap.
The management fee is payable to an affiliate of Landlord.
An administration or supervisory fee is charged in addition to a property management fee.
Law-compliance capital costs are includable regardless of when the underlying law took effect.
Capital costs are amortized over a fixed period shorter than the item's useful life.
preferred_language: Operating Expenses shall include property management fees payable to a property manager, including any affiliate of Landlord, not to exceed three percent (3%) of all Operating Expenses, and no separate administration or supervisory fee shall be charged in addition thereto. Operating Expenses shall include the cost of additions or alterations made by Landlord to comply with applicable laws and regulations only to the extent such laws first become effective after the date of this Lease, or to the extent such additions or alterations result in a net reduction of overall Operating Expenses, and any such cost shall be amortized on a straight-line basis over the useful life of the item for federal income tax purposes.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings from a single counterparty lease negotiation, both rated high significance and pointing the same direction, so the direction is clear but the sample is thin.
matching_clause_names: Operating Expenses - Capital Improvements for Law Compliance

title: Expansion of Premises and Addition of Space
where_to_look: Premises granting clause, and any amendment or addendum adding space, expansion premises, or adjusting rent.
required: Add expansion space by amendment that folds it into the single defined Premises, coterminous with the existing term at a stated adjusted rent.
fallback: Accept a separate addendum for the added space where it expressly incorporates all terms of the existing lease and states its own commencement and expiration dates.
escalate_if: Expansion space is added without attorney review where the rent adjustment or the boundary of the added area is left undefined.
flag_if: The amendment adds space but does not fold it into the single defined term Premises.
The added space is described only by square footage with no exhibit or depiction attached.
The expansion space carries a term or expiration date different from the existing lease.
Rent is not restated or adjusted for the added square footage.
The document creates a second numbered lease instead of amending the existing one.
preferred_language: Expansion of Premises and Adjustment of Rent. Effective as of the Expansion Commencement Date, the Premises under the Lease are expanded to include the additional space depicted on Exhibit A (the "Expansion Premises"), and the Expansion Premises together with the Premises demised under the Lease shall be deemed the "Premises" for all purposes of the Lease. The Expansion Premises are leased on all of the terms and conditions of the Lease, the term for the Expansion Premises is coterminous with the Term, and Base Rent is increased by the amount set forth herein for the Expansion Premises.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties, both high significance and consistent in direction, though the evidence base is thin.
matching_clause_names: Premises / Expansion of Premises and Adjustment of Rent

title: Grant of Tenancy and Landlord Reserved Rights
where_to_look: Demise or granting clause, and the landlord reserved-rights provisions covering entry, relocation, and remarketing.
required: Obtain an express demise with common-area use rights, strike any unilateral relocation right, and allow Landlord entry only on reasonable prior written notice.
fallback: Accept relocation only to space of substantially similar area and quality, at Landlord's sole cost, on not less than sixty days' prior written notice. Accept entry for emergency, cleaning, inspection, and for remarketing only after Tenant has given notice to terminate.
escalate_if: Relocation is permitted with no minimum notice, no size and quality equivalence, or at Tenant's cost, or Landlord may reconfigure the Premises at will.
flag_if: Landlord may relocate Tenant or change the location of the Premises without a stated minimum notice period.
Relocation and moving costs are silent or charged to Tenant.
Landlord may enter the Premises at any time or without prior notice outside emergencies.
Landlord may show or remarket the Premises before Tenant has given notice to terminate.
There is no express granting or demise clause conveying the Premises and common-area rights to Tenant.
preferred_language: Landlord hereby demises and lets to Tenant the Premises for the Term, together with the non-exclusive right for Tenant and its employees, agents, and invitees to use the Common Areas and Common Facilities. Landlord shall have no right to relocate Tenant or to change the location of the Premises during the Term. Landlord may enter the Premises only upon not less than twenty-four hours' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and solely for inspection, repair, or maintenance, except in the case of a bona fide emergency. Landlord shall exercise all reserved rights so as not to interfere materially with Tenant's use and occupancy of the Premises.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings across 3 counterparties, all showing landlord-side reserved rights inserted into the signed document and accepted with guardrails rather than resisted, so the direction is consistent but the stakes and leverage are moderate.

title: Permitted Use and Scope of Use Restrictions
where_to_look: Permitted Use definition in the term sheet or basic lease provisions, and the Use covenant section of the lease.
required: Draft the permitted use to cover Tenant's actual operations plus all uses ancillary or incidental thereto.
fallback: Accept a use clause naming Tenant's specific operations where it expressly extends to ancillary and incidental uses, and Landlord's consent to additional compatible uses is not unreasonably withheld.
escalate_if: Any use outside a single narrow named purpose is an immediate event of default, or the use clause is narrower than Tenant's planned operations.
flag_if: The permitted use names a single activity with no ancillary or incidental uses.
The clause says the Premises may be used for no other purpose and provides no consent mechanism for added uses.
The permitted use is carried over from a term sheet and is narrower than Tenant's planned operations.
Landlord consent to a change in use is subject to Landlord's sole or absolute discretion.
Exceeding the permitted use is an event of default with no notice or cure period.
preferred_language: Use. Tenant shall use the Premises for general office, warehousing, manufacturing and light industrial purposes, for all uses ancillary or incidental thereto, including administrative, sales, research and support activities, and for any other lawful use permitted by applicable zoning and approved by Landlord, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. No change in use shall constitute a default so long as the use remains within the foregoing.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties with a consistent direction toward broader use language, though the sample is small and one change was of moderate significance only.

title: Landlord Delivery-Condition Standard and Delivery Deadline Remedies
where_to_look: The Delivery Date definition and the delivery/condition-of-premises section, including term-sheet condition and improvement fields.
required: Require Landlord to deliver the Premises broom clean, in good order and repair, free of latent defects, legally compliant and free of Hazardous Substances by a fixed outside date, with the Rent Commencement Date extended one day for each day of late or non-conforming delivery.
fallback: Accept a delivery standard limited to broom clean, good working order and compliance with law, with Landlord curing latent defects, legal violations and Hazardous Substances within a commercially reasonable time after notice, so long as the Rent Commencement Date still shifts day for day for delayed delivery.
escalate_if: Landlord delivers strictly as-is with no cure obligation, or the Rent Commencement Date and rent obligations run from a fixed date regardless of when Landlord actually delivers.
flag_if: The lease delivers the Premises as-is with no stated delivery-condition standard.
The Delivery Date definition does not require delivery in the condition required under the lease.
Landlord has no obligation to cure latent defects, legal violations or Hazardous Substances after notice.
No outside date is fixed for Landlord's delivery of possession.
The Rent Commencement Date is a fixed calendar date that does not shift for delivery delay.
preferred_language: Landlord shall deliver the Premises to Tenant on the Delivery Date broom clean, in good order, condition and repair, free from latent defects, in compliance with all applicable laws and free from Hazardous Substances. Landlord shall cure any latent defect, violation of law or Hazardous Substances condition within a commercially reasonable time after receipt of notice from Tenant. If Landlord fails to deliver possession of the Premises in the condition required under this Lease by the Outside Delivery Date, the Rent Commencement Date shall be extended by one day for each day of delay.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties, one high-significance and detailed and one fragmentary, so the direction is consistent but the evidence base is thin.
matching_clause_names: Delivery of Premises (Section 1.01 "Delivery Date" definition and new Section 2.01)

title: AS-IS Acceptance and Carve-Outs for Landlord's Continuing Obligations
where_to_look: AS-IS acceptance and condition-of-premises provisions, including tenant-improvement and extension-term amendments.
required: Make each AS-IS acceptance expressly subject to all Landlord obligations under this Lease and the Existing Lease.
fallback: Accept AS-IS with a written carve-out naming Landlord's delivery-condition duties and its maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations.
escalate_if: Never accept AS-IS language that waives, limits, or supersedes Landlord's maintenance, repair, or replacement obligations.
flag_if: AS-IS acceptance appears with no carve-out for Landlord's obligations.
The only carve-out points to a single exhibit rather than the whole Lease.
Landlord disclaims any obligation to repair, replace, or improve the Premises, Building, or Common Areas.
An extension or amendment restates AS-IS acceptance without preserving the Existing Lease obligations.
AS-IS acceptance is paired with a waiver of all representations and warranties.
preferred_language: Tenant accepts the Premises in their AS-IS, WHERE-IS condition, without representation or warranty by Landlord, subject in all respects to Landlord's delivery-condition obligations and to Landlord's maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations set forth in this Lease, in any amendment hereto, and in the Existing Lease, all of which survive and are not waived, limited, or superseded by Tenant's acceptance of the Premises.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings across 2 counterparties, consistent direction with one high-significance instance.
matching_clause_names: Condition of Premises / Extension Term Acceptance

title: Environmental and Legal-Compliance Condition Representations
where_to_look: Premises condition and delivery sections, landlord representations, and any environmental or compliance-with-laws clause.
required: Require the landlord to represent the premises are law-compliant and free of hazardous material, and to indemnify for pre-existing conditions.
fallback: Accept a representation limited to the landlord's actual knowledge at delivery if the landlord keeps the duty to remediate pre-existing hazardous material and legal violations at its own cost after notice.
escalate_if: Never accept as-is delivery that leaves Marmon responsible for hazardous material or legal violations it did not cause.
flag_if: The premises are delivered as-is with no landlord representation on condition or legal compliance.
No clause allocates responsibility for hazardous material existing before the commencement date.
The tenant must comply with environmental laws with no corresponding landlord representation.
The landlord's environmental representation carries no remediation or indemnity obligation.
Surrender or restoration obligations reference environmental condition without carving out pre-existing contamination.
preferred_language: Lessor represents and warrants that, as of delivery, the Premises, common areas, and all appurtenances comply with all applicable laws, including environmental laws, and are free from hazardous material and latent defects. Lessor shall cure any latent defect, violation of law, or hazardous material condition within a commercially reasonable time after notice from Lessee. Lessor shall defend, indemnify, and hold Lessee harmless from any violation of law or hazardous material in, on, or under the Premises that pre-dates the Commencement Date or is not caused by Lessee.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings from a single counterparty and one lease, both rated high significance and moving in the same direction, so the direction is clear but the sample is narrow.

title: Allocation of Repair, Maintenance, and Building-Systems Responsibility
where_to_look: Repairs and maintenance sections of the lease and any addendum, plus the maintenance line in the term sheet.
required: Require Landlord to maintain, repair and replace the structure, roof, exterior walls and shared building systems, and to test fire protection systems on a documented recurring schedule.
fallback: Accept Tenant responsibility for routine interior maintenance and for systems exclusively serving the Premises, provided Landlord keeps the foundation, structural elements, roof, exterior walls and fire protection systems, and Tenant may inspect Landlord's testing records on request.
escalate_if: Tenant is made responsible for repairing or replacing the roof, foundation, structural elements, or the building's fire protection and sprinkler systems.
flag_if: Maintenance is assigned to Tenant with no carve-out for structure, roof, or exterior walls.
Landlord's repair obligation omits HVAC, plumbing, or utility lines that do not exclusively serve the Premises.
The lease is silent on who maintains and tests sprinkler and fire protection systems.
Landlord has no obligation to keep written testing records or make them available to Tenant.
Tenant is charged with capital repairs or replacement of building systems at its own cost.
preferred_language: Landlord shall, at its sole cost and expense, maintain, repair and replace the foundation, structural elements, exterior walls, roof, and all building systems and utility lines that do not exclusively serve the Premises, including all sprinkler and fire protection systems, in good order and repair. Landlord shall test all fire protection systems no less than quarterly and shall maintain written records of such testing for review by Tenant upon request. Tenant's maintenance obligations are limited to routine maintenance of the interior of the Premises.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties, both high significance and both shifting responsibility to the landlord, so the direction is consistent but the sample is small.

title: Tenant Improvement Scope, Allowance Use, and Landlord Approval Standard
where_to_look: Tenant Improvements or Alterations section, including allowance use and landlord sign-off on construction drawings.
required: Give Tenant sole discretion over whether to make improvements necessary or desirable for its operations, with Landlord approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.
fallback: Accept Landlord approval of plans and drawings on a reasonableness standard with a stated response deadline, provided Tenant still decides which permitted improvements to pursue and may apply the unused allowance to them.
escalate_if: Landlord holds sole or absolute discretion over Tenant improvements, or unused allowance is forfeited or reverts to Landlord on Landlord's refusal to approve.
flag_if: Landlord approval of improvements or construction drawings is stated without a reasonableness standard.
Approval is subject to Landlord's sole, absolute, or unfettered discretion.
Permitted improvements are limited to those strictly necessary for Tenant's operations.
No outside deadline governs Landlord's response to submitted plans or drawings.
Landlord, rather than Tenant, decides whether additional improvements are made or allowance is drawn.
preferred_language: Tenant may make any improvements to the Premises that Tenant deems necessary or desirable for the conduct of its business, and the decision whether to make any such improvements, and to apply any unused Tenant Improvement Allowance to them, shall be in Tenant's sole discretion. Such improvements shall be performed in accordance with construction drawings approved in writing in advance by Landlord, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings from a single counterparty and a single transaction, consistent in direction but medium significance, so treat as provisional until more leases confirm it.

title: Fit-Out Access, Timing, Cost, and Landlord Non-Liability During Works
where_to_look: Fitting-out availability and possession clauses, and the fit-out works schedule covering access, hours, and cost.
required: Secure a defined rent-free and service-charge-free fit-out period with access from execution and landlord approval of fit-out plans not to be unreasonably withheld. The landlord remains liable for loss caused by its own works during that period.
fallback: Accept tenant-borne fit-out cost, restricted working hours, and the landlord's right to carry out its own concurrent works, provided the landlord's exculpation excludes negligence and wilful acts and the fit-out period extends day for day for landlord-caused delay.
escalate_if: A blanket waiver of all tenant claims against the landlord for the landlord's own works during fit-out, or rent running before the premises are available for fit-out.
flag_if: Fit-out availability or possession clauses are marked 'Not Applicable' or omitted from the lease.
Rent or service charge is payable during the fit-out period.
The tenant waives all claims against the landlord for the landlord's works during the fit-out period.
Landlord approval of the tenant's fit-out plans carries no reasonableness qualifier.
Landlord-caused delay does not extend the fit-out period.
preferred_language: The Landlord shall make the Demised Premises available to the Tenant for the Tenant's fitting-out works from the date of this Agreement, subject only to approval of the Tenant's fitting-out plans by the relevant authorities and the Landlord, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed, and no rent or service charge shall be payable during the Fitting-Out Period. The Landlord may carry out its own works during the Fitting-Out Period provided that it does not materially interfere with the Tenant's fitting-out works, the Fitting-Out Period is extended day for day for any resulting delay, and the Landlord remains liable for loss and cost caused by such works.
confidence_note: Based on 2 high-significance findings arising from a single counterparty's lease template, consistent in direction but narrow in sourcing, so treat as provisional outside comparable landlord-form tenancy agreements.
matching_clause_names: Availability of Demised Premises for Fitting-Out Works / Possession and Tenant's Fitting-Out Works

title: Insurance Requirements, Coverage Form, and Waiver of Subrogation
where_to_look: Property and liability insurance sections and the damage-liability clause, including any amendment revising them.
required: Require property coverage written on a Causes of Loss - Special Form basis and a mutual waiver of subrogation in both parties' policies, with each party liable only for damage it causes negligently, recklessly, or intentionally.
fallback: Accept an equivalent all-risk property form and a waiver of subrogation running in Marmon's favor, so long as losses that are insured or required to be insured stay carved out of each party's damage liability.
escalate_if: The waiver of subrogation runs only in the counterparty's favor, or Marmon bears damage liability for losses the other party was required to insure.
flag_if: The property insurance section requires Broad Form Causes of Loss or fire and extended coverage rather than Special Form.
Neither party's property policies are required to contain a waiver of subrogation.
The waiver of subrogation is written in favor of the landlord alone.
The damage-liability clause leaves Marmon liable for losses covered by the other party's insurance.
An amendment broadens required coverage to reach added inventory, personnel, or space.
preferred_language: Each party shall maintain property insurance covering its own property at the Premises written on a Causes of Loss - Special Form basis, or its equivalent. Each party shall be liable to the other for all damage to the property of the other caused negligently, recklessly, or intentionally by that party or its agents, employees, or invitees, except to the extent the loss is insured, or is required to be insured under this Agreement, and subrogation is waived under the insuring party's policy. Each party shall cause its property insurance policies to contain a waiver of subrogation in favor of the other party.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties moving in the same direction, one of which carries a low document-similarity caveat, so treat this rule as provisional.

title: Indemnity and Liability for Damage Caused by a Party or Its Contractors
where_to_look: Indemnity and hold-harmless provisions, and alterations or damage-liability terms in leases and license agreements.
required: Make the indemnity mutual and fault-based, limited to each party's own negligence and willful misconduct.
fallback: Accept a one-way indemnity limited to Marmon's negligence and willful misconduct, with claims caused by the landlord or its agents carved out and consequential damages excluded.
escalate_if: The indemnity reaches claims caused by the landlord's own negligence, or applies without regard to fault and without any liability cap.
flag_if: The indemnity obligation runs in one direction only.
The trigger is any claim arising out of the occupancy rather than the indemnitor's fault.
Marmon is made liable for damage caused by anyone present with its express or implied permission.
The clause sweeps in fines, attorney fees, and consequential damages without limitation.
Consent to alterations or IT and cabling work is refusable in the landlord's absolute discretion with all costs on Marmon.
preferred_language: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other party and its officers, employees and agents from and against third-party claims, losses, damages, and reasonable attorneys' fees to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party or its employees, contractors, or agents. Each party's indemnity obligation is reduced in proportion to the negligence of the indemnified party. Neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special, or punitive damages.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties pointing the same direction, but both were one-way indemnities inserted and accepted rather than fought over, so this rule is provisional.

title: Default, Notice-and-Cure Periods, and Landlord Remedies
where_to_look: Default and remedies sections, and any provision that conditions a tenant right on the absence of default.
required: Require written notice and a cure period before any default arises, and strike all landlord self-help lockout rights.
fallback: Accept shorter cure periods of five days for rent and twenty days for other defaults, and accept lockout rights only after those periods expire and only with written notice delivered to Tenant.
escalate_if: Never accept a default or lockout right exercisable without written notice, or a waiver of tenant protections under the governing property code.
flag_if: The lease excuses Landlord from giving written notice of nonpayment of Rent.
Landlord may change the door locks or otherwise bar Tenant from the Premises.
The default section states that it supersedes or overrides the governing property code.
A default carries consequences before the applicable notice period has run.
Landlord is released from liability for wrongful eviction, conversion, or forcible entry claims.
preferred_language: Default. Tenant shall not be in default under this Lease unless Landlord has delivered written notice of the alleged default to Tenant and Tenant has failed to cure it within ten (10) days after such notice for a monetary default or thirty (30) days after such notice for any other default. No right or remedy of Landlord conditioned on a Tenant default shall arise or be exercised before those notice and cure periods expire, and Landlord shall not change the locks to or otherwise deny Tenant access to the Premises without a judicial order of possession. This Section does not waive any protection afforded Tenant under applicable law.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings across 2 counterparties moving in the same direction, though the evidence is thin and one change was a narrow notice-period insertion, so treat as provisional.

title: Surrender, Restoration and Post-Termination Survival
where_to_look: Surrender and return-condition provisions, including alteration-removal obligations and post-termination survival language.
required: Limit the return condition to broom-clean and good repair, excepting ordinary wear and tear, casualty damage, and anything Landlord is obligated to repair or maintain. Require any alteration-removal demand to be made in writing at the time the alteration is installed.
fallback: Accept a removal demand made in writing when Landlord approves the alteration plans, and accept survival of the surrender obligations for up to twelve months, so long as casualty damage and Landlord's own repair obligations remain carved out of the return condition.
escalate_if: Landlord requires restoration of casualty damage or of Landlord-maintained systems, imposes removal demands first raised at move-out, or insists on indefinite survival.
flag_if: The return condition is excepted only for ordinary wear and tear.
Landlord may demand removal of alterations at or after lease expiration.
Tenant must restore the Premises to original, shell, or base-building condition.
The surrender provision survives expiration or termination with no stated end date.
Move-out conditions sit in a schedule Landlord can revise unilaterally.
preferred_language: Upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall surrender the Premises broom-clean and in good condition and repair, excepting ordinary wear and tear, damage by fire or other casualty, and any condition Landlord is obligated to repair, maintain or replace under this Lease. Tenant shall remove its personal property, and shall remove an alteration only if Landlord requested such removal in writing at the time such alteration was installed, and shall promptly repair any damage caused by such removal. The provisions of this Section shall survive the expiration or termination of this Lease for a period of six (6) months.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings drawn from a single lease with one counterparty, all moving the same direction across return condition, removal timing, and survival, so the direction is clear but the sample is thin.

title: Scope of Services: Covered Equipment and Service Locations
where_to_look: Scope of Services and Definitions provisions, plus any attached equipment schedule or service-location schedule.
required: Define covered equipment and every service location in attached schedules that are integral parts of the agreement and amendable only by mutual written agreement.
fallback: Accept a narrower equipment definition limited to owned and leased units, provided the location schedule remains amendable by mutual written agreement and closure or relocation of a listed mobile unit requires only written notice rather than consent.
escalate_if: Unilateral amendment of the equipment or location schedules by the counterparty, or treatment of a mobile unit closure or relocation as breach or default.
flag_if: Covered equipment is referenced in general terms with no defining clause.
Service locations are fixed in the body of the agreement instead of an amendable schedule.
A schedule can be amended by one party without the other party's written consent.
Closing or relocating a mobile service unit is an event of breach or default.
Third-party equipment is either excluded outright or admitted with no approval requirement.
preferred_language: Services shall be performed on Covered Equipment at the locations designated in Schedule A. Covered Equipment means units owned, finance leased, net leased or full service leased by Customer, and units belonging to other entities approved by Customer, that are delivered to a designated location for repair or inspection. Remote Services shall be provided from Service Trucks and from the mobile unit locations listed in Schedule B, to the extent of the capabilities of those mobile units. Schedules A and B are integral parts of this Agreement and may be amended only by written agreement of the parties. Closure or relocation of a mobile unit shall not constitute a breach of this Agreement, provided that Provider gives Customer written notice of the closure of any mobile unit listed in Schedule B.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings from a single counterparty within one rail car maintenance arrangement, both medium significance and pointing the same direction, so treat this rule as provisional until more deals confirm it.
matching_clause_names: MARATHON Rail Cars Definition & Service Locations (Schedule A/B)
Mobile Unit Closure / Service Trucks Definition

title: Equipment Ownership, Site Cost Allocation, and End-of-Term Purchase Option
where_to_look: Facilities, equipment ownership, and termination sections covering site cost allocation and end-of-term equipment.
required: Equipment title and maintenance cost stay with the party that supplied it, and any end-of-term purchase option prices at mutually agreed fair market value.
fallback: Accept a counterparty purchase option on Marmon-supplied equipment where the price is fair market value, the option expires within a fixed window, and Marmon may remove and redeploy equipment the counterparty declines to buy.
escalate_if: Never accept transfer of equipment title at no cost or at book value, or maintenance and casualty cost for equipment Marmon does not own.
flag_if: The agreement transfers equipment title on termination without a stated purchase price.
A purchase option is priced at book value, original cost, or a fixed formula rather than fair market value.
The purchase option has no expiration date or exercise window.
Marmon must maintain, repair, or insure equipment owned by the counterparty.
Site utilities, permits, structures, or track infrastructure are not assigned to a named party at each location.
preferred_language: Each party shall retain title to all equipment it provides under this Agreement and shall bear the cost of maintaining, repairing, and insuring such equipment, except for costs arising from damage or loss caused by the negligence of the other party. Upon termination, the providing party shall offer the other party an option, exercisable within one hundred eighty (180) days, to purchase such equipment at fair market value as mutually agreed by the parties, taking into account original purchase price and equipment condition. If the option is not exercised within that period, the providing party may remove and redeploy the equipment without further obligation.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings from a single contract with one counterparty, consistent in direction but a narrow evidence base.

title: Regulatory Certification, Procedures, and Site-Safety Compliance
where_to_look: Performance-standards, procedures, and certification provisions, and standalone site-safety or hazard-warning articles.
required: Limit compliance to named regulatory standards and the certifications listed in the schedules, and require advance written notice before revised counterparty procedures bind.
fallback: Accept compliance with counterparty procedures as revised where changes apply prospectively only and any revision that increases cost, scope, or time entitles the service provider to an equitable adjustment of pricing and schedule.
escalate_if: Certification or site-safety obligations reach beyond the contracted service scope, or regulatory noncompliance is excluded from the liability cap.
flag_if: Compliance obligations incorporate the counterparty's internal procedures including future modifications.
Certification requirements are stated without reference to a schedule or a defined service category.
Revised procedures take effect without advance written notice to the service provider.
Hazard-warning language imposes duties on personnel without any corresponding site-information obligation on the counterparty.
Regulatory noncompliance triggers immediate termination or is carved out of the limitation of liability.
preferred_language: Service Provider shall perform the Services in accordance with the standards, practices, and manuals of the regulatory bodies identified in the Schedules and shall maintain the certifications expressly listed therein. Service Provider's obligation to comply with Customer's internal procedures extends only to procedures delivered to Service Provider in writing and applies prospectively. Where a revision to such procedures increases Service Provider's cost, scope, or time of performance, the parties shall equitably adjust the affected pricing and schedules.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings from a single agreement with one counterparty, and the underlying text reads as an operational rail-car servicing arrangement rather than a lease, so the direction is consistent but the sample is thin and the rule is provisional.
